content: The American Dental Association (ADA) is a professional organization in the United States that advocates for oral health care and the field of dentistry. It was founded in 1859 and currently has over 152,000 members, making it the largest and oldest national dental association in the world. The ADA is headquartered in Chicago, Illinois, and also maintains an office in Washington, D.C. The organization is dedicated to promoting good oral health among the public and representing the interests of dental professionals. The ADA publishes a monthly journal called the Journal of the American Dental Association (JADA), which features articles on dental research, clinical studies, and advancements in the field. The association also produces other publications, such as the ADA News and the ADA Guide to Dental Therapeutics. Additionally, the ADA oversees the Commission on Dental Accreditation, which is recognized by the U.S. Department of Education as the accrediting body for dental education programs in the United States. The ADA was established in August 1859 in Niagara Falls, New York, by 26 dentists representing various dental societies across the country. Today, the organization includes 55 constituent (state and territorial) and 545 component (local) dental societies. The ADA employs over 400 staff members at its Chicago headquarters and Washington, D.C. office. The Paffenbarger Research Center (PRC), located on the campus of the National Institute of Standards and Technology (NIST) in Gaithersburg, Maryland, is part of the ADA Foundation. Scientists at the PRC conduct research in areas such as clinical studies, dental chemistry, polymer chemistry, and cariology. The ADA has established rigorous guidelines for the testing and advertising of dental products. In 1931, the organization awarded its first Seal of Acceptance, a program that continues today with participation from approximately 350 manufacturers and over 1,300 products receiving the seal. The ADA's administrative body, the Board of Trustees, includes the President, President-elect, two Vice Presidents, and 17 trustees representing the 17 trustee districts in the United States. The legislative body, known as the House of Delegates, consists of 460 delegates representing 53 constituent societies, five federal dental services, and the American Student Dental Association. The House of Delegates convenes annually during the ADA's annual session. The ADA has 11 councils that serve as policy-recommending agencies. Each council focuses on specific areas of interest and provides recommendations to the Board of Trustees and the House of Delegates. The ADA formally recognizes nine specialty areas within dentistry: dental public health, endodontics, oral and maxillofacial pathology, oral and maxillofacial surgery, orthodontics and dentofacial orthopedics, pediatric dentistry, periodontics, prosthodontics, and oral and maxillofacial radiology. The ADA library houses an extensive collection of dental literature, including approximately 33,000 books and 17,500 bound journal volumes. It also subscribes to over 600 journal titles. The ADA Foundation, the charitable arm of the organization, provides grants for dental research, education, scholarships, and access to care. It also offers charitable assistance programs, such as relief grants for dentists and their dependents who are unable to support themselves due to injury, medical conditions, or advanced age, as well as grants for victims of disasters. Significant milestones in the history of the ADA include the following: In 1840, the first dental college, the Baltimore College of Dental Surgery, was established, and the American Society of Dental Surgeons was formed. In 1859, 26 dentists met in Niagara Falls, New York, to form the ADA. In 1860, the first ADA constitution and bylaws were adopted. In 1922, the organization was renamed the American Dental Association. In 1930, the ADA established the Council of Dental Therapeutics to evaluate dental products and launched the Seal of Acceptance program in 1931. In 1950, the ADA endorsed water fluoridation and worked with Congress to establish National Children's Dental Health Day. In 1970, the ADA began publishing ADA News. In 1979, the Commission on Dental Accreditation was established. In 1991, Dr. Geraldine Morrow became the first female president of the ADA. In 2002, Dr. Eugene Sekiguchi became the first minority president of the ADA. In 2003, the ADA launched the Give Kids a Smile program as part of National Children’s Dental Health Month. The ADA continues to play a vital role in advancing the field of dentistry, promoting oral health, and supporting dental professionals through education, research, and advocacy.
